lead.headline: China confirms Xi will meet Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November, though Beijing resists a nuclear arms pact
lead.short: China has confirmed that Xi Jinping will hold the first three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. Trump wants a new nuclear arms treaty that includes China, but Beijing, with a smaller arsenal than Washington and Moscow, has long signalled it is not ready to join one.

why.text: The world's three biggest nuclear powers have had no arms limits between them since February, and this is the first time all three leaders will sit down together.

more: New START, signed in 2010 and extended in 2021, capped the US and Russia at 1,550 deployed strategic warheads and 700 long-range missiles and bombers, and allowed up to 18 inspections a year. It lapsed in February. Trump rejected Russia's offer to extend it, demanding a "new, improved and modernised" deal that includes Beijing.

China worries that any pact could limit its nuclear build-up while it still trails the other two. The talks will also cover the US-Israeli war with Iran, according to Reuters. Trump's Asia trip comes after his party lost both houses of Congress in this month's midterms.

update.new: China confirms the date and signals it will resist a treaty.
update.front: The three-way summit is now confirmed for Thursday, and China is already setting limits.

seconds.headline: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.29% in October as fuel and power prices jump almost 33%
seconds.short: India's wholesale price inflation rose to 12.29% in October from 11.39% in September, provisional data released on Monday show. Fuel and power drove it, with prices in the group up 32.84% on a year earlier, against 25.85% in September. Inflation in primary articles rose to 9.24%, while manufactured products eased slightly to 9.54%.

why.text: Higher costs for businesses feed through to shop prices, and with retail inflation already above 6% the RBI is under pressure to raise rates again.

more: Inflation in mineral oils rose to 45.57% from 40.02%, and in crude petroleum and natural gas to 70.80% from 57.32%. Electricity turned positive at 8.06%, from minus 0.43% in September. The food index, about a quarter of the basket, eased slightly to 8.58% from 8.66%. The wholesale price index itself rose to 113.3 from 112.5.

The government named mineral oils, crude and gas, electricity, food, basic metals, chemicals, textiles and plastics among the main contributors. Retail inflation reached 6.09% in October, above the RBI's 6% ceiling for the first time in two years, and the central bank's policy committee meets on 2 to 4 December.

update.front: After retail prices crossed the RBI's limit, wholesale inflation has hit 12.29%.

seconds.headline: Jensen Huang discusses a comeback at Nvidia as 165,000 sign a letter for his return, but Bessent wants an outsider
seconds.short: Jensen Huang has discussed returning to Nvidia with people close to him, the Financial Times reported, four days after he resigned. An open letter asking the board to "bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts" has more than 165,000 signatories, including Elon Musk. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia should look outside for its next chief.

why.text: The fight over Nvidia's leadership now pits Silicon Valley against the administration, days before the company reports earnings.

more: One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return and would try to win White House support. "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the effort had Huang's backing.

"They need a dramatic shake-up," Bessent said on Fox News, calling on Nvidia to explain whether it knowingly let its most advanced chips reach China. "Nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese," he said, adding that what mattered was "whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the US export restrictions".

update.new: Huang talks of a comeback; Bessent wants an outsider.
update.front: Four days after quitting, Huang is discussing a return to Nvidia.

seconds.headline: India defend 209 to beat New Zealand by 22 runs at Mount Maunganui and win the ODI series 3-1
seconds.short: India beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui on Sunday to win the series 3-1, two days after being bowled out for 89 at the same ground. India made 209 in 42.1 overs, then bowled New Zealand out for 187 in the 49th over, with Axar Patel taking the last wicket.

why.text: It is a rare ODI series win in New Zealand, achieved under a stand-in captain with a young pace attack, days before the Tests.

more: Arshdeep Singh dismissed Will Young, caught by a diving Ruturaj Gaikwad at square leg, and bowled Nick Kelly, while Mohammed Siraj removed Tim Seifert and Finn Allen. Debutant Yash Thakur and Auqib Nabi took Michael Bracewell and Foxcroft in consecutive overs, and Naman Dhir had Santner caught at mid-wicket.

Shreyas Iyer, captaining in place of Shubman Gill, kept his pace bowlers going rather than turning to spin until late, and Axar finished it by dismissing Jacob Duffy. Virat Kohli dropped Foxcroft at second slip. Matt Henry and Gurnoor Brar had been released to prepare for the Tests, the first of which starts in Wellington at 03:30 IST on Thursday.

update.new: India won the fifth ODI and the series.
update.front: India bounced back from 89 all out to win the series 3-1.

stories.headline: Modi leaves for Manila for the ASEAN-India and East Asia summits, and a Quad meeting with Trump may follow
stories.short: Narendra Modi left on Monday for Manila to attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on 17 November, at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. "Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India's Act East Policy," he said. A Quad summit with Trump in Manila is also expected.

why.text: A Quad meeting in Manila would be the first time Modi and Trump meet in person since the US-India trade dispute.

more: Modi said he wanted to build on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with ASEAN and give "further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity". He called the East Asia Summit an important platform for dialogue and said he looked forward to discussing peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are expected to join Modi for the annual Quad summit in Manila, though there is no official word, The Hindu reported. It would be the first Quad summit held in a country outside the group, bringing together the leaders of India, the US, Australia and Japan.

stories.headline: Zelensky urges the US and Elon Musk to lift speed limits on the Starshield service Ukraine uses to stop drones
stories.short: Volodymyr Zelensky said speed restrictions on Starshield, a military-grade satellite service built by Musk's Starlink and supplied by the US government, are hurting Ukraine's ability to stop Russian missiles and drones. "The protection of lives and Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter directly depends on this," he said, urging both to be "on the right side of history".

why.text: Winter attacks on the power grid are Russia's main weapon against Ukrainian civilians, and Starshield helps shoot the drones down.

more: Ukraine uses the ordinary Starlink service for battlefield communications and Starshield to intercept drones in its airspace. The speed problem was first identified in October and led to conflicting accounts: Musk said the US government was responsible because it controls Starshield. The issue has been rumbling on for weeks; the BBC asked the White House and Starlink for comment.

Zelensky said he had asked officials "to work as closely as possible" with the US government and Musk's company. The appeal came days after he said US negotiators had floated Nato membership for Ukraine in return for giving up the Donbas.

stories.headline: A ULA Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes after launch and loses 40 of Amazon's Leo internet satellites
stories.short: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket "suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight" and failed to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit, the company said, reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history. It was the first of 38 launches Amazon has bought from ULA for Leo, its rival to SpaceX's Starlink.

why.text: It sets back Amazon's effort to catch Starlink, which already has a huge lead in satellite internet, including in India.

more: Leo has struggled to get off the ground, with only a small part of the satellites it needs to challenge Starlink in orbit so far. ULA, a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, launched the rocket from Space Launch Complex 41 and said it was still unclear what went wrong.

Amazon said it still had confidence in its launch partner. "There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01," it posted on X. "ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan."

briefs.headline: Microsoft says its next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console that can play PC games, not a PC that plays console games

stories.headline: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid with 10 men, ending the world champions' 43-match unbeaten run
stories.short: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid on Sunday, holding on with 10 men to end the world champions' 43-match unbeaten run and take top spot in their Nations League group on goal difference. England led 3-0 inside an hour through a Harry Kane penalty, Ezri Konsa's header and Ben White's shot, before Elliot Anderson was sent off.

why.text: It is Spain's first defeat since March 2024, and Real Madrid's Bellingham, Huijsen and Cucurella were all involved.

more: Kane's penalty, after Pau Cubarsí fouled him, was his 93rd England goal on his 127th appearance. Konsa headed in Declan Rice's corner eight minutes after half-time, and White finished a counter-attack set up by Jude Bellingham. It was England's record 10th straight away win. Spain, who had paraded their World Cup trophy before kick-off, did not manage a shot on target in the first half.

Anderson was shown a straight red 25 minutes from time for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Mikel Oyarzabal scored the penalty past James Trafford, recalled in place of Jordan Pickford. Spain scored again and kept attacking through four minutes of stoppage time, but England held on.
